messages:
camille: Heads up — I'm prototyping a retention-aware dynamic sampler that uses route + customer.tier to decide head vs tail, plus a retention budget signal to avoid blowing storage.
raj: Nice. Curious how you plan to surface the budget and override per-customer.
morgan: Quick note: OTEL spans already have attributes we can use. route -> http.route, customer -> tenant.id, tier -> tenant.tier. We should standardize keys.
camille: Agreed. Plan: sampling decision uses (route, tier) bucket, and we attach metadata: sample.reason and retention_until. Tail sampling kicks in for high-latency/error windows.
tess: How do we avoid heavy tail sampling for giant tenants during blasts? that's our main cost risk.
camille: Two levers: 1) per-tenant retention budget (tokens/day) that drains by exported bytes; 2) adaptive decay that reduces tail sample rate if budget low. Also burst-protection by capping tail-sampled spans per-minute.
telemetry-bot: exporter: signalfx-exporter v2 deployed to canary (rg: telemetry-canary)
lydia: For exporters, we should expose a soft quota so exporters drop lower-priority spans before disk fills. Prefer to emit metrics showing dropped spans per-exporter.
raj: UX: product wants ability to set 'preserve' rules in Console (e.g., always keep spans for route /payments when tier=enterprise). Can we map that to config keys?
camille: Yes — Console rule -> policy with matchers -> policy_id. Runtime reads policies from config service and updates sampler quickly. Example matcher: "http.route =~ ^/payments" AND "tenant.tier == 'enterprise'".
morgan: Implementation detail: we should do sampling in two phases: head (probabilistic) on ingress where we can reduce QPS, then tail (deterministic based on full trace) in collector. Head labels should carry head_decision and head_sample_rate.
tess: That means collectors need stateful tail buffer to decide which traces to keep. Memory cost?
camille: We'll keep a small LRU ring per-route and per-tenant for candidate traces, evict oldest when full. Tuneable size per-tier.
lydia: Console UX: show a 'retention budget burn' graph per-tenant, and an 'expected monthly storage' calc when changing rates. Ops needs quick rollback button.
raj: Also add an emergency fallback: if exporter backpressure hits, auto-switch to 'minimal' sampler (errors + 1% tail) and send paging alert.
sam: +1 to fallback. Also add deterministic sampling for GDPR opt-outs: set sample.decide=0 for tenant flags.
camille: POC config snippet:
```
sampler:
  matchers:
    - expr: "http.route =~ '^/payments' && tenant.tier == 'enterprise'"
      action: preserve
  default_head_rate: 0.02
  tail_policy:
    base_rate: 0.001
    budget_scaling: true
    max_per_minute: 500
```
morgan: Good. For metrics: report sampled_spans, dropped_by_budget, tail_promoted, head_chosen. Keep tags route,tier.
tess: let's schedule 30m sync to finalize collector memory limits and console controls.
camille: Yep — I'll open a short RFC next with diagrams and sample telemetry charts. Assigning followups: @morgan collector memory, @lydia console metrics, @raj fallback/alerts.
raj: I'll draft the alert runbook. :+1:
lydia: I'll mock console widgets and share tomorrow. :eyes:
telemetry-bot: incident: exporter-throttle-alert triggered for cluster telemetry-prod at 2026-03-19T22:14:03Z
camille: Thanks — that's exactly why we need the auto-fallback. Meeting: Thu 10am to iterate.
